items.title: Make contentHash order independent of locale by replacing localeCompare with a code-unit compare
items.body:
## Problem
`packages/protocol/src/pack.ts:32` and `:38` sort files and assets with `a.relPath.localeCompare(b.relPath)` before hashing. `localeCompare` depends on the runtime's ICU/locale data, so the same set of files can sort differently (e.g. `_` vs letters, case, accents, Cyrillic paths) on two machines or Node builds. The hash is the parcel's integrity/identity value (`manifest.contentHash`), produced on one machine (sync/reports) and consumed on another (worker/agent), so a locale difference yields a different hash for identical content.

## Proposed change
Replace both comparators with a locale-independent one, e.g. `(a, b) => (a.relPath < b.relPath ? -1 : a.relPath > b.relPath ? 1 : 0)`, via a tiny shared helper in `pack.ts`. Add a test in the protocol package's pack tests asserting a fixed expected hash for a file set containing mixed-case, underscore, digit and Cyrillic paths, and that input order does not matter. Note: this changes hashes for existing parcels only when their paths sorted differently under the old comparator; document that in the PR description.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `contentHash` no longer calls `localeCompare`.
- [ ] A test pins the exact hash for a mixed-case/underscore/Cyrillic path set and passes.
- [ ] A test shows shuffled input produces the same hash.
- [ ] `npm test` in `packages/protocol` passes; roundtrip test still passes.

items.title: Verify manifest contentHash against extracted files in extractArchive
items.body:
## Problem
`buildArchive` stamps `contentHash` into every manifest (`packages/protocol/src/pack.ts:57-61`), but `extractArchive` (`pack.ts:75-110`) only checks that the manifest exists and its `schemaVersion` (`pack.ts:103-107`). The hash is never recomputed, so a truncated, tampered or partially-corrupted parcel that still unzips is silently accepted and then applied to a working branch or de-anonymized back into a project. The field exists but provides no protection.

## Proposed change
After extraction, if `manifest.contentHash` is a string, recompute `contentHash(files, assets)` and throw a clear error on mismatch (`Parcel ${entryName} failed integrity check: contentHash mismatch`). If the field is absent (pre-hash parcels) skip the check silently. Do this after the locale-independent sort fix so hashes agree across machines. Add tests in the protocol package: round-trip passes; a parcel whose file entry was altered after build throws; a manifest without `contentHash` still extracts.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A modified file entry in an otherwise valid zip makes `extractArchive` throw.
- [ ] Parcels without `contentHash` still extract.
- [ ] `roundtrip.test.ts` and sync/reports tests that use `extractArchive` still pass.
- [ ] New tests cover match, mismatch and missing-field cases.

items.title: Treat empty-string provider env vars as unset in resolveOpenAiCompatibleConfig
items.body:
## Problem
`worker/src/providers.ts:65-67` uses `env[defaults.baseUrlEnv] ?? defaults.defaultBaseUrl` and `env[defaults.modelEnv] ?? defaults.defaultModel`. `??` only falls back on undefined, so `OPENAI_BASE_URL=` or `OPENAI_MODEL=` set to an empty string (common with docker-compose/Swarm `${VAR:-}` passthrough or a blank line in an env file) yields an empty base URL or model name. The job then fails later with an opaque fetch/URL error instead of using the documented default. The API key check at `providers.ts:59` already uses a falsy test, so the three values are handled inconsistently. The same function backs chat turns via `worker/src/chatProviders.ts:19`.

## Proposed change
Use a small helper (`const nonEmpty = (v?: string) => v?.trim() || undefined`) and apply it to base URL, model and API key (a whitespace-only key should also count as unset). Add tests in worker's providers test file: empty/whitespace base URL and model fall back to defaults; whitespace-only key throws the existing 'is not set' error; explicit values are preserved and trimmed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `OPENAI_BASE_URL=''` resolves to `https://api.openai.com/v1`; same for deepseek and qwen defaults.
- [ ] Empty model env resolves to the default model.
- [ ] Whitespace-only API key throws.
- [ ] `npm test` in `worker` passes.

items.title: Reject non-numeric schemaVersion in assertSchemaVersion instead of silently accepting it
items.body:
## Problem
`packages/protocol/src/manifest.ts:22-36` only guards `schemaVersion === undefined` and `schemaVersion > PROTOCOL_SCHEMA_VERSION`. A manifest with `schemaVersion: null`, `NaN`-producing values, or a non-numeric string makes the comparison false (`null > 2`, `'abc' > 2`), so the parcel is accepted as if valid and the 'newer than understood' protection is bypassed. A numeric string such as `"3"` is coerced and rejected only by accident. Manifests come from untrusted JSON (`pack.ts:88` casts `JSON.parse` output with `as M`).

## Proposed change
Add an explicit check: if `schemaVersion` is not a non-negative integer (`Number.isInteger(v) && v >= 0`), throw `${entryName} has an invalid schemaVersion (${JSON.stringify(v)})`. Keep the `undefined` warn-only path for legacy parcels. Add tests to the protocol manifest tests covering null, string, NaN, negative, float, undefined (warns), current and newer versions.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `null`, `'3'`, `NaN`, `-1`, `1.5` all throw with a clear message.
- [ ] `undefined` still only warns; current version and older integers pass.
- [ ] A version newer than `PROTOCOL_SCHEMA_VERSION` still throws the existing upgrade message.
- [ ] `npm test` in `packages/protocol` passes.

items.title: leakScan: skip hostname findings that are the domain of an email and make line lookup linear
items.body:
## Problem
1. `packages/protocol/src/leakScan.ts:102-118`: every email such as `bob@corp.internal` is reported as an `email` finding (`EMAIL_RE`, line 25) and again as a `hostname` finding for `corp.internal` (`HOSTNAME_RE`, line 35), because the hostname pass runs over the full content with no knowledge of email spans. Users see two warnings per leak, inflating the count in `formatLeakFindings` (`leakScan.ts:136-147`) and pushing real findings past the default `limit = 20`.
2. `lineAt` (`leakScan.ts:91-97`) rescans the content from index 0 for every match, making a scan O(matches x file size). A large minified or generated file with thousands of token/hostname matches goes quadratic, and this runs in sync/reports on every push.

## Proposed change
- Collect email match ranges first and skip any hostname match whose start index falls inside one.
- Precompute newline offsets once per target and resolve line numbers by binary search (or a single running counter, since matches arrive in index order per pass).
Add tests in the protocol leakScan tests: an email yields exactly one finding (kind `email`); a standalone hostname still yields a `hostname` finding; line numbers are unchanged for a multi-line sample; a large input (e.g. 50k matches) completes within a loose time bound.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `a@corp.internal` produces one `email` finding and no `hostname` finding.
- [ ] A hostname elsewhere on the same line is still reported.
- [ ] Existing line-number expectations in leakScan tests are unchanged.
- [ ] `lineAt` no longer loops from 0 per match.
- [ ] `npm test` in `packages/protocol` passes.
